drivingQuestion: What does the baraita's seemingly obvious statement that everyone is obligated in sukka come to teach?
outcomeNote: the baraita's mention of priests is justified: it rules out a partial-exemption inference, on the model of travelers

segments.he: הַכֹּל חַיָּיבִין בְּסוּכָּה, כֹּהֲנִים לְוִיִּם וְיִשְׂרְאֵלִים. פְּשִׁיטָא! אִי הָנֵי לָא מִחַיְּיבִי, מַאן מִיחַיְּיבִי?
segments.en: § The Gemara discusses several other cases where a mishna or baraita states that everyone is obligated in a particular mitzva. A baraita teaches: «Everyone is obligated in» the mitzva of «sukka,» including «priests, Levites, and Israelites.» The Gemara asks: Isn’t that «obvious? If these» people «are not obligated» to perform the mitzva, then «who is obligated» to perform it?

segments.he: כֹּהֲנִים אִיצְטְרִיכָא לֵיהּ, סָלְקָא דַּעְתָּךְ אָמֵינָא: הוֹאִיל וּכְתִיב ״בַּסֻּכּוֹת תֵּשְׁבוּ״, וְאָמַר מָר ״תֵּשְׁבוּ שִׁבְעַת יָמִים״ כְּעֵין תָּדוּרוּ, מָה דִּירָה — אִישׁ וְאִשְׁתּוֹ, אַף סוּכָּה — אִישׁ וְאִשְׁתּוֹ, וְהָנֵי כֹּהֲנִים הוֹאִיל וּבְנֵי עֲבוֹדָה נִינְהוּ — לָא לִיחַיְּיבוּ.
segments.en: The Gemara answers: «It was necessary for» the halakha to mention that «priests» are obligated to fulfill this mitzva, as it might «enter your mind to say» that «since it is written: “In sukkot shall you reside» seven days” (Leviticus 23:42), one can argue as follows: «The Master said» that this teaches: «Reside seven days as you dwell» in your permanent home: «Just as» in the case of «dwelling,» a «man and his wife» typically reside together, «so too,» the mitzva of «sukka» must be performed by «a man and his wife» residing together. «And» with regard to «these priests, since they are» occupied «with» the Temple «service» during the Festival and are not free to dwell in the sukka together with their wives, perhaps they «should not be obligated» in the mitzva of sukka.

segments.he: קָא מַשְׁמַע לַן: נְהִי דִּפְטִירִי בִּשְׁעַת עֲבוֹדָה, בְּלֹא שְׁעַת עֲבוֹדָה חַיּוֹבֵי מִיחַיְּיבִי, מִידֵּי דְּהָוֵה אַהוֹלְכֵי דְרָכִים, דְּאָמַר מָר: הוֹלְכֵי דְרָכִים בַּיּוֹם פְּטוּרִין מִן הַסּוּכָּה בַּיּוֹם, וְחַיָּיבִים בַּלַּיְלָה.
segments.en: Therefore, the baraita «teaches us» that this is not so, as «although» priests are «exempt at the time of» the Temple «service, when it is not the time of» Temple «service they are obligated, just as is» the halakha «with regard to travelers. As the Master said» in a baraita: «Travelers» who are on the move «during the day are exempt from» the mitzva of «sukka during the day but are obligated at night,» as they are not traveling at that time.

moves.cueHe: הכל חייבין בסוכה, כהנים לוים וישראלים
moves.summary: opens the series of baraitot phrased הכל חייבין... כהנים לויים וישראלים by citing the one about sukka
moves.about: brings the baraita that everyone — priests, Levites and Israelites — is obligated in the mitzva of sukka

moves.summary: objects that the baraita is self-evident — if these are not obligated, who is?
moves.about: why the baraita has to say that priests, Levites and Israelites are obligated in sukka, when there is nobody else who could be obligated

moves.summary: answers that the clause was needed for the case of priests
moves.about: the clause about priests is necessary, to forestall the inference that priests are exempt from sukka

moves.summary: floats the hava amina that since sukka is דירה of man and wife, priests busy with the service would be exempt
moves.about: the verse ‏בסכות תשבו שבעת ימים‎ is brought as the ground of the hypothetical exemption

moves.summary: concludes that priests are exempt only during the service itself and obligated otherwise
moves.about: the travelers' baraita is deployed as the precedent supporting the resolution that an intermittent exemption does not remove the obligation altogether

moves.cueHe: מידי דהוה אהולכי דרכים, דאמר מר
moves.summary: supports the conclusion with the baraita of travelers, exempt by day and obligated at night
moves.about: what the baraita's mention of priests actually teaches — they are exempt only at the hour of the Temple service and obligated the rest of the time
